intro: Electrolyte Corrections is an in-app clinical reference for the treatment and work-up of common paediatric electrolyte disturbances — hyper- and hypocalcaemia, hyper- and hyponatraemia, hyper- and hypokalaemia, hypoglycaemia, hypomagnesaemia, and hypophosphataemia. Each disturbance card lists first-line treatment options and a relevant diagnostic work-up, and where applicable links directly to PediAid's own correction calculators, such as free water deficit, sodium correction, and potassium correction. Per the source, every value on the card is a verbatim transcription, and the guide is intended for use by qualified clinicians only.
indications: Quickly reviewing first-line treatment options for a specific electrolyte disturbance at the bedside
Identifying the appropriate diagnostic work-up to determine the cause of an electrolyte abnormality
Jumping directly from a disturbance summary into the matching PediAid calculator, such as sodium or potassium correction
Cross-checking adjunct therapies such as albumin, bicarbonate, and THAM dosing formulas
Reviewing linked diagnostic calculators such as anion gap, serum osmolality, and corrected sodium for hyperglycaemia
method: This is a structured reference card rather than a single calculator — it lists treatment and work-up bullet points for nine electrolyte disturbances, plus adjunct correction formulas transcribed from the source, such as the free water deficit formula "FWD = 0.6 (wt) ([Na]/140 − 1)" and the sodium deficit formula "Na deficit (mEq) = (Na_goal − Na_meas) × wt × 1.2." Each disturbance section links out to a matching interactive calculator elsewhere in the app (e.g., Sodium Correction, Potassium Correction, Calcium Correction, Magnesium Correction, Phosphate Correction, Free Water Deficit, Dextrose Bolus) for the actual computation.

faqs.q: What electrolyte disturbances does this reference cover?
faqs.a: Hypercalcaemia, hypocalcaemia, hypernatraemia, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypokalaemia, hypoglycaemia, hypomagnesaemia, and hypophosphataemia.

faqs.q: Does this guide perform calculations itself?
faqs.a: The guide itself is a treatment and work-up reference; calculations are performed by the linked calculator tools it points to, such as sodium correction, potassium correction, and free water deficit calculators.

faqs.q: What formula does the guide give for free water deficit?
faqs.a: It states "FWD = 0.6 (wt) ([Na]/140 − 1)" alongside the rule of thumb "4 mL FW/kg = ↓ Na 1 mEq/L."

faqs.q: What work-up does the guide suggest for hyponatraemia?
faqs.a: It lists urine and serum osmolality, urinalysis, urine electrolytes, CMP, lipids, and water restriction if SIADH is suspected.

faqs.q: What other diagnostic calculators does this guide link to?
faqs.a: Anion Gap, Serum Osmolality, and Corrected Sodium (for hyperglycaemia) calculators are listed as "Linked diagnostic calculators."
